{
  "summary": "Escapes embedded newline characters as hex sequences within the logging subsystem while centrally preserving a single trailing newline terminator. Adds a line-splitting utility and updates intentional multiline logging call sites—including exceptions, UI message boxes, and wallet diagnostics—to emit each line as an individual log entry. Adds unit tests and functional test cases verifying newline escaping in rejected RPC method calls and wallet names.",
  "problem": "Untrusted inputs such as rejected RPC method names or wallet names can contain newlines that pass through logging unescaped, allowing restricted RPC users or callers to forge arbitrary log lines in debug.log. Node operators and automated log-monitoring tools can be misled by injected lines disguised as node errors or status messages.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Restricted RPC users and callers of createwallet or restorewallet can inject newlines through rejected methods or wallet names, and global log escaping preserves them, making forged lines look like node messages.'",
    "Author provides a reproducer demonstrating that passing a newline followed by an 'ERROR: ConnectTip: ConnectBlock ...' string in an unauthorized RPC call creates a forged error entry in debug.log."
  ],

evidence: PR description: 'Restricted RPC users and callers of createwallet or restorewallet can inject newlines through rejected methods or wallet names, and global log escaping preserves them, making forged lines look like node messages.'
Author provides a reproducer demonstrating that passing a newline followed by an 'ERROR: ConnectTip: ConnectBlock ...' string in an unauthorized RPC call creates a forged error entry in debug.log.
result.scope_notes: Modifies central logging escaping in src/logging.cpp and updates multiple call sites (noui, exception handler, wallet) to split multiline messages.
result.card: This pull request escapes embedded newlines as hex sequences in the logger to prevent untrusted user inputs from forging log lines. Currently, inputs like rejected RPC method names or wallet names can inject arbitrary lines into debug.log, which could mislead operators or automated monitoring systems. The author provides a concrete reproducer showing a restricted RPC user forging an ERROR: ConnectTip log line. To preserve readability, the PR introduces a line-splitting helper and updates multiline logging sites like exceptions and wallet messages to log each line separately. No dependencies are noted.
